subject: Post-call: Ramsey pilot - urgent capacity & deployment path (hosted -> dedicated/VPC)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramsey <alex.ramsey@ramseyinc.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Ramsey pilot — immediate capacity concern and options

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary of what we heard
- Pilot hit a sustained 8–10x request spike during yesterday's batch ingestion window, leading to elevated tail latencies and transient 5xx throttles on the hosted environment.
- Your SREs are okay with a short-lived capacity change if it avoids user-facing errors this week.
- Primary constraints: PCI-adjacent traffic, compliance review for data residency, and procurement timeline for reserved capacity.

Options we discussed (high level)
1) Short-term Hosted mitigation — increased request throttles + temporary burst quota to reduce 5xx; fastest but brittle under repeating surges.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) — predictable throughput, ~3–5 business days to provision if we fast-track.
3) Private (VPC) deployment — longer lead time (2–4+ weeks) for networking and controls, but aligns with your compliance roadmap.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Can you confirm risk tolerance: symptomatic fix (Hosted burst) vs. contract/commitment for Dedicated? If Dedicated, what target RPS and P99 latency SLO are you aiming for?
- Please loop in procurement/legal if we should start a draft SOW. I attached the pilot_capacity_runbook.pdf for your SREs.

I'll hold on the dedicated provisioning step until I have confirmation from you that Ramsey wants to pursue reserved capacity; otherwise we can apply a temporary hosted burst while we scope dedicated.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0112

Attachment: pilot_capacity_runbook.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

From: Alex Ramsey <alex.ramsey@ramseyinc.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Ramsey pilot — immediate capacity concern and options

Thanks, Priyom — appreciate the crisp summary. Quick answers: 
- We need reliability this week. The business impact is material (checkout failures for premium users).
- Short-term hosted burst is acceptable only if it guarantees no further 5xx for the next 72 hours; we need a clear rollback plan.
- Long-term we prefer Dedicated, but procurement needs a draft SOW to start internal approvals.

Can you give a firm timeline to have Dedicated ready (provision + validation) if we greenlight it today? Also, can Redwood support a Private VPC pathway if our compliance team insists?

– Alex
Alex Ramsey
VP, Platform Engineering | Ramsey Inc.
alex.ramsey@ramseyinc.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

Looping you both in — Ramsey just asked for a firm timeline for Dedicated if they greenlight today, and they want a guaranteed 72-hour hosted mitigation as a fallback. Key items we need to assemble quickly: 
- Vivek: a minimal Dedicated configuration (gpu type, instance count, expected sustained RPS, expected P99) and validation plan (smoke tests, perf window).

Let's aim for a short internal call tomorrow (20–30 min) and an external one with Alex by EOD tomorrow. I'll offer hosted burst coverage in the interim if we can set clear surge limits.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Ramsey pilot — host -> dedicated? urgent timeline

Priyom / Lauren — quick technical estimate below. This is a minimal canary config; we can scale after validation.
- Recommended GPU: 2 x A100-80GB equivalent (quantized weights) for the pilot dedicated pool.
- Expected sustained throughput: ~900–1,200 RPS for typical prompt mix; P99 target ~180–220ms with batch tuning.
- Provisioning timeline if we fast-track: 48–72 hours to get capacity reserved + 24 hours for smoke validation (total ~3 business days).
- Migration notes: we can route a fraction of traffic to the dedicated pool (canary) and fall back to hosted. KV cache warmup will require a short ramping window — estimate 6–12 hours for 80% cache hit.

Immediate ask from my side
- Provide representative request profile (token distribution and concurrency) so I can refine batch sizing and expected token/sec.
- Confirm whether data must stay in a VPC (if yes, dedicated in VPC or Private deployment is required).

I'll draft a short validation checklist and a runbook for the canary steps and attach it to the SOW.

— Vivek
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Ramsey pilot — immediate next steps and proposed path (hosted burst + fast-track Dedicated)

Alex — quick status update and concrete asks so we can move quickly: 

What we can do immediately (today)
- Apply a temporary hosted burst configuration for 72 hours to cap throttles and give your team breathing room. We'll set a strict surge limit and monitoring alerts; we will require emergency contact details and a rollback trigger.

If you greenlight Dedicated (recommended)
- Redwood can fast-track provision: target timeline 48–72 hours + 24 hours validation (total ~3 business days). Vivek attached an initial capacity estimate; we'll refine after you share representative traffic samples.
- Lauren has prepared a draft SOW and SOC2 evidence for procurement. Links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/RDW-2347 (deal), https://www.docusign.com/templates/RC-2347-SOW (SOW template).

Requested actions from Ramsey
1) Reply to this thread with explicit approval for temporary hosted burst (72 hours) or confirmation to proceed directly to Dedicated.
2) Upload a tokenized sample of your typical request (anonymized) to the shared drive link so Vivek can finalize batch sizing.
3) If procurement wants SOW changes, please flag by EOD Mon so Lauren can iterate.

If helpful, I can schedule a 20-minute runbook walkthrough with your SREs this afternoon. We want to make sure you avoid further customer-facing errors this week.

Thanks — Priyom
